from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Wrap a signal around a circle.",
            "Adjust frequency to match the signal.",
            "Center of mass shifts away.",
            "This spike reveals the frequency.",
            "The Fourier transform acts as prism."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: The Center of Mass", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Create points representing a signal (e.g., a simple wave form)
        signal_points = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(50)])
        for i, p in enumerate(signal_points):
            t = i / 50 * TAU
            p.move_to(self.grid["C3"] + 0.5 * np.array([np.cos(t), np.sin(t), 0]))
        self.play(FadeIn(signal_points))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Rotate(signal_points, angle=PI, about_point=self.grid["C3"], run_time=2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        centroid = Dot(color="#FF00FF")
        centroid.move_to(self.grid["C3"])
        self.play(FadeIn(centroid))
        
        # Animate shifting
        shift_vector = np.array([1, 1, 0])
        self.play(
            signal_points.animate.shift(shift_vector),
            centroid.animate.shift(shift_vector),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        spike = Line(centroid.get_center(), centroid.get_center() + UP * 1, color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(spike))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Time domain shows how things happen.", "Frequency domain shows what things are.", "Fourier transform bridges these two views."]
        self.setup_layout("Time Domain vs. Frequency Domain", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup objects
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda t: np.sin(2 * np.pi * t) + 0.5 * np.sin(4 * np.pi * t), x_range=[-2, 2], color="#00FF00")
        bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=np.random.rand(), width=0.5, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=1) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.place_in_area(wave, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_in_area(bars, 'D1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(bars))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(wave.animate.scale(0.5).move_to(self.grid['B2']), bars.animate.scale(0.5).move_to(self.grid['E2']))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: Real-World Filtering", ["Frequencies identify specific sound types.", "Unwanted noise has unique high frequencies.", "Remove these to clear your audio."])
        
        # Create graphs
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C2')
        
        # Signal function (noisy)
        noisy_signal = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(10 * x), color='#FF0000')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color('#FF0000')
        self.add(axes, noisy_signal)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color('#FFFFFF')
        # Represent low-pass filter (shaded box)
        filter_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color='#FFFFFF', fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(filter_box, 'C5')
        self.play(FadeIn(filter_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color('#00FF00')
        cleaned_signal = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * x), color='#00FF00')
        self.play(Transform(noisy_signal, cleaned_signal), FadeOut(filter_box))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: The Intuitive Hook: The Smoothie Analogy (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of decomposition. Just as a smoothie can be deconstructed into its original ingredients, any complex signal can be broken down into simple sine waves.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Berry-Banana-Kale' smoothie being separated back into three distinct piles of fruit.

sections.title: Prerequisite Recap: Rotating Vectors (0:45-1:30)
sections.content: Briefly revisit Euler’s Formula (e^ix = cos x + i sin x). Explain how a signal can be visualized as a point rotating around a circle at different frequencies.
sections.example: An animation of a vector spinning; the 'shadow' cast on the X-axis creates a sine wave.

sections.title: The Mechanism: The Center of Mass (1:30-3:00)
sections.content: Explain the Fourier Transform as a tool that 'wraps' a signal around a center point at a specific frequency. If the frequency matches the signal's component, the center of mass shifts away from the origin.
sections.example: A complex wave of a chirping bird 'wrapped' around a circle. When the rotation speed matches the bird's pitch, the center of mass spikes—revealing the frequency.

sections.title: Key Concept: Time Domain vs. Frequency Domain (3:00-4:00)
sections.content: Contrast the Time Domain (where things happen) with the Frequency Domain (what things are made of). Emphasize that the Fourier Transform is the bridge between these two views.
sections.example: Side-by-side animation: A piano keyboard playing a chord (Time Domain) vs. a bar chart showing the specific notes being played (Frequency Domain).

sections.title: Application: Real-World Filtering (4:00-5:00)
sections.content: Demonstrate why this matters. If we can see the frequencies, we can remove the ones we don't want (Noise Cancellation).
sections.example: A smartphone character filtering out 'background construction noise' from a voice recording by simply erasing the high-frequency spikes in the Frequency Domain.
